issue_context.title: support sql_safe_updates variable
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**

preventing updating or deleting the whole table by accident

**Describe the feature you'd like:**

Like MySQL [sql_safe_updates](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_sql_safe_updates):

> If this variable is enabled, UPDATE and DELETE statements that do not use a key in the WHERE clause or a LIMIT clause produce an error. This makes it possible to catch UPDATE and DELETE statements where keys are not used properly and that would probably change or delete a large number of rows. The default value is OFF.

An example:

```sql
MySQL(root@127.0.0.1:test) > set @@sql_safe_updates = 1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)

MySQL(root@127.0.0.1:test) > delete from t;
ERROR 1175 (HY000): You are using safe update mode and you tried to update a table without a WHERE that uses a KEY column.
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered:**

N/A

**Teachability, Documentation, Adoption, Migration Strategy:**

N/A

review_comments: Should we just check the `best` plan instead of every plan? The `range scan` plan may not be chosen as the chosen one.
If the optimizer chooses a full-scan as the best plan, but actually some other range-scans can be used, we shouldn't return the error in this case.
